低音薩魯梭風採用金屬外殼構造，主要由黃銅或其他銅合金製成，確保樂器的耐用性和共鳴: The bass sarrusophone has a metal body, mainly of brass or another copper alloy, which gives it durability and resonance. Inside, the bore is conical, to optimise timbre and intonation. The mouthpiece uses a double reed, usually of cane, joined to a metal mouthpipe. The keywork is of nickel silver or stainless steel, for responsive control of intonation. The whole instrument is precisely machined and polished for the best acoustic performance.
低音薩魯梭風擁有渾厚深沉的音色，具有金屬樂器特有的溫暖而略帶沙啞的質感。其音域寬: The bass sarrusophone has a full, deep timbre, with the warm, slightly husky quality particular to metal instruments. Its range is wide, covering the bassoon's range up to F4; the low register is heavy and powerful, the middle register relatively warm and full. Because it uses a double reed and a conical bore, the instrument resonates well and can produce a penetrating sound. Compared with the bass saxophone, the bass sarrusophone sounds darker and more archaic, with a stronger metallic quality; compared with the bassoon, its tone is brighter and more sonorous. Altogether it is an instrument of distinctive timbre and great expressiveness, able both to carry a heartfelt melody and to give solid support to the bass part.
低音薩魯梭風是薩魯梭風樂器家族中的低音成員，屬於金屬雙簧錐形管孔木管樂器。音調為: The bass sarrusophone is the bass member of the sarrusophone family, a metal double-reed woodwind with a conical bore. It is pitched in B♭, and its range is almost the same as the bass saxophone's, covering the bassoon's range up to F4. Historically it was made mainly by its inventor, Pierre-Louis Gautrot, in the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries, and also by his successors Couesnon & Co., by Evette & Schaeffer, and by the Orsi firm in Milan. Today it can only be bought to order from Orsi.
低音薩魯梭風為薩魯梭風家族的低音成員，屬金屬雙簧圓錐管氣鳴樂器，調性為降B。其製: The bass sarrusophone is the bass member of the sarrusophone family, a metal double-reed conical-bore aerophone pitched in B-flat. Its manufacture was concentrated in the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries, mainly by its inventor Pierre-Louis Gautrot and his successor Couesnon & Co., with Evette & Schaeffer and the Milan firm Orsi also taking part. Today it can be ordered only from Orsi.
